heading: Batch normalization can accelerate training, but its benefits depend on the setting
definition: adding batch normalization makes networks gain accuracy faster and tolerate higher learning rates than the same networks without it (sigmoid networks on MNIST, VGG on CIFAR-10, Inception on ImageNet; Ioffe & Szegedy 2015; Santurkar et al. 2018). Residual networks can train as fast and stably without normalization using Fixup's initialization, scalar biases and multipliers (Zhang, Dauphin & Ma 2019).
summary: Several independent groups reproduce faster accuracy gains with batch normalization, but general claims of acceleration and higher learning-rate tolerance are contested. Fixup offers an alternative for residual networks, though its speed and stability also depend on the training setup.

suggested_status.by_scale: No parameter-count scale can be assigned: versions.V6.studies_by_size contains only 'not stated'. The conditional supporting results and contested general wording cannot be mapped reliably to toy, <1B, 1–10B, 10–100B or >100B from these counts.
suggested_status.reason: The unrestricted wording has explicit reversals: arXiv:1904.03441#R2 reports poor small-batch BN learning, and arXiv:1905.02161#R3–R6 reverses learning-rate tolerance. Conditional acceleration is reproduced beyond the originals: arXiv:1903.00925#R3–R5 gives steps to common predictive-accuracy targets, and arXiv:2003.04887 supplies a later Fixup target-accuracy comparison. Counts: versions.V6.verdicts.supports.studies = 49, limits_scope.studies = 21 and challenges.studies = 8. C describes the broad wording; the records also support R2 for condition-specific acceleration, without establishing universal BN benefits or universal Fixup stability.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched initialization and optimizer comparisons that locate the batch-size and learning-rate boundaries; complete Fixup versus BN under a common recipe with maximum-rate sweeps and elapsed time to common accuracy; parameter-count reporting sufficient for scale-specific judgments.

source.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

original_result.setup: The original study compared Inception with batch-normalized variants on ImageNet.
original_result.result: Adding batch normalization alone reduced steps to 72.2% validation accuracy from 31.0 million to 13.3 million. BN-x5 and BN-x30, which also changed the learning rate and training recipe, reached that target in 2.1 million and 2.7 million steps, respectively.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An isolated higher-learning-rate Inception/ImageNet comparison holding the remainder of the training recipe fixed, including a quantitative maximum-stable-rate boundary.
untested.basis: arXiv:1502.03167's untested line and arXiv:1502.03167#R4–R5 identify combined recipe changes. arXiv:1903.00925#R4 supplies matched reduced-rate speed evidence: Section 4.4 reports that removing BN required lowering Inception-v2's learning rate, and all Inception-v2 comparisons use that reduced rate; Appendix A.4 gives base learning rate 0.006. No systematic BN-versus-baseline maximum-stable-rate sweep is reported. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.training and versions.V6.main_rows_by_operation aggregate operations without identifying maximum-rate sweeps; they do not close this specific gap.

untested.what: A common-recipe quantitative maximum-stable-learning-rate comparison of complete Fixup and BN that jointly establishes matched learning speed and stability.
untested.basis: The untested lines of arXiv:2003.04887 and arXiv:2101.08692 exclude quantitative matched stability boundaries. arXiv:2002.10674 tests FixupCore rather than complete Fixup. Original Fixup reports speed and stability without a quantified common boundary. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.training and versions.V6.rows_by_state provide aggregate coverage, not this joint comparison.

untested.what: Matched elapsed time to a common accuracy target for Fixup versus BN, and for the reported PointNet and ImageNet BN step-count comparisons.
untested.basis: Fixup evidence uses epochs or qualitative curves; arXiv:2101.08692 explicitly leaves accuracy-versus-time or iteration learning curves untested. arXiv:1903.00925#R3–R5 count steps. The DeepWeeds elapsed-time result concerns another task and does not close these gaps. counts: versions.V6.rows_by_evidence_form and versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.training do not distinguish elapsed time from updates.

untested.what: Matched-learning-rate Kodak image-fitting experiments isolating BN from the larger selected learning rate.
untested.basis: The supplied extension arXiv:2407.17834#R1–R2 uses normalized initial learning rate 0.01 and unnormalized initial learning rate 0.0002 in Section 5.1. No matched-rate Kodak convergence comparison is reported in the relevant experiment. This gap is inferred from the experimental configuration; explicit acknowledgment of the gap was not found. The supplied results are from the extension rather than the named CVPR paper. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.training records aggregate training coverage without a matched-rate classification.

untested.what: Parameter-count-resolved evidence supporting comparisons across the catalog's size buckets.

wording_issues.phrase: adding batch normalization makes networks gain accuracy faster
wording_issues.issue: The direction depends on initialization, activation and batch size. Shared AP2 initialization produces oscillatory BN training, EOC-initialized deep networks have worse curves and longer training time, and small-batch or deep activation conditions can underperform or fail. MNIST ReLU-GPN training accuracy is 33.28% without BN and 11.42% with BN.

The ordering reverses in some DenseNets without warmup and on Adversarial Spheres. Large BNGD tolerance gains require separate parameter-group rates. Separately, one-layer MNIST shows similar best first-epoch performance for GD and BNGD, a challenges result for that condition. SSD tolerance depends on BN placement; its comparison trains on VOC 2007+2012 trainval and evaluates on VOC 2007 test, with base learning rate 0.001 and tenfold rate 0.01.

wording_issues.phrase: than the same networks without it
wording_issues.issue: The largest original ImageNet speedups change other recipe components. Some later comparisons change selected learning rates or optimizers, add BN to existing GN and WS, or compare BN against LN. In large-batch ImageNet ResNet-50, BCN+WS versus GN+WS isolates incremental BN addition while retaining GN and WS; BCN+WS versus GN also changes WS. These comparisons do not all measure BN addition to an otherwise unnormalized network.

Some support measures first-epoch loss, training NLL, noisy-sample loss or image-fitting PSNR. One-layer MNIST shows similar best first-epoch performance for GD and BNGD, a challenges result for that condition. Fixed-budget accuracy also differs from time to a common accuracy target. The noisy-label study's aggregate clean-set Figure 4 row remains cannot_determine; broader clean/noisy support comes from separate Appendix C.3 text.

Steps, epochs and elapsed time are distinct measures. PointNet and ImageNet results count steps to accuracy targets. Feedback-alignment CNNs on CIFAR-10 show earlier, smoother test-accuracy convergence over steps under separately tuned SGD or AdamW recipes, with a 50,000-step budget and early stopping for convergence or failed runs; no numerical convergence-speed comparison is stated. For COCO-pretrained Faster RCNN ResNet-101 on DeepWeeds, convergence improves from 50K iterations to 47K steps with default BN decay 0.99 and epsilon 0.001. The elapsed-time comparison belongs to the separately tuned epsilon 0.01 setting.

wording_issues.phrase: as fast and stably without normalization
wording_issues.issue: Fixup speed support coexists with depth- and recipe-specific failures and reduced learning-rate requirements. Epochs to an accuracy target do not jointly quantify equivalent stability or elapsed-time speed.

wording_issues.phrase: using Fixup's initialization, scalar biases and multipliers
wording_issues.issue: FixupCore tests an initialization component rather than the complete recipe. For ResNet20 on CIFAR-10, Figure 12a measures validation error versus convolution-weight learning rate after 19 epochs across 20 seeds; the overall protocol specifies 20 epochs. This is an endpoint learning-rate sweep, and FixupCore becomes unstable at µ = 0.05. Output scaling, ZerO and binary-network replacements are different recipes. The reported Transformer Fixup divergence concerns an architectural extension.

method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:1904.03441, BN improves full-batch MNIST training in a four-layer MLP with 100 neurons per hidden layer, but barely learns at batch size 2 while the plain network learns well; learning rates are selected separately. The outcome is training loss over iterations, with figure-only values. The small-batch CIFAR-10 underperformance comes from arXiv:2108.01110's five-layer CNN at batch size 2. In 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.033135, UNet trains faster with BN at batch size 1 using separately optimized rates. In arXiv:1907.09539, single-example convolutional fitting succeeds with channel normalization equivalent to BN.

BN-derived initialization narrows sigmoid-network differences, while AP2-derived initialization produces oscillatory BN training. EOC-initialized deep networks worsen after BN addition. Deep fully connected activation conditions include both unfavorable outcomes and a favorable ordinary-SELU/CIFAR-10 condition: in 200-layer networks at the same 100-epoch budget, training accuracy is 29.23% without BN and 46.47% with BN. ResNet-110 with scale-1 initialization fails without BN but learns with BN.

WideResnet 28-10 benefits from BN learning-rate tolerance, while some DenseNets reverse the ordering without warmup. With warmup, BN DenseNets train above .1 while non-BN variants diverge. The depth of the DenseNet reversal is not specified.

method_sensitivity.factor: Parameter-group rates, weight projection and BN scale
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:1810.00122, separate BN-parameter and other-weight rates enlarge the stable weight-rate range. In arXiv:1812.03981's modified VGG, the scale-invariant group includes kernels and concatenated BN scale/shift parameters before the last BN; only the last BN's scale/shift parameters are scale-variant. With the latter rate fixed at 0.1 and scale-invariant rates 0.01–100, ordinary BN training reaches zero loss while projected training stalls at larger rates. Ordinary BN training also reaches zero with unified rates; this study establishes no separate-versus-unified enlargement. Mean-field stability boundaries depend on γ. The LeNet/ResNet comparison separately sets convolution-weight and other-parameter rates. Its Figure 12a measures validation error versus convolution-weight rate after 19 epochs across 20 seeds, within a 20-epoch protocol; FixupCore becomes unstable at µ = 0.05.

As mechanism context, arXiv:1901.10159's ResNet-32/CIFAR-10 comparison reports much slower loss optimization with population statistics than with mini-batch statistics, using a learning rate divided by 100 and at least 400 initial steps at learning rate 0. Both conditions retain normalization, so this does not determine V6's BN-versus-no-BN effect or relative learning-rate tolerance. Separately, arXiv:1806.02375 reports that alternating statistic refresh lowers ResNet-110's reported highest achievable rate relative to standard BN; this comparison also retains normalization.

Final BN improves reported ResNet optimization. For VGG16/CIFAR-100 at learning rate 0.01, best accuracy within ten epochs is 34.81% with Weight Mean and 38.39% with MimicNorm, which adds final BN. Weight Mean versus no normalization does not isolate a BN effect. Removing the second PNNH learner BN instead accelerates initial loss convergence. SSD trained on VOC 2007+2012 trainval and evaluated on VOC 2007 test uses base rate 0.001 and tenfold rate 0.01. Head-only BN fails at 0.05, while backbone or whole-network BN converges. Without BN, SSD fails at 0.01 and 0.05 but converges at 0.001.

Inception-v2 variants share the reduced rate required by the unnormalized baseline and still differ in steps to target accuracy. In the supplied Kodak image-fitting extension, arXiv:2407.17834, normalized coordinate networks use initial learning rate 0.01 versus 0.0002 without normalization; training PSNR curves and faster convergence are reported under these unequal rates. These results are not independently verified for the named CVPR paper. For COCO-pretrained Faster RCNN ResNet-101 on DeepWeeds, the reduction from 50K iterations to 47K steps uses default BN decay 0.99 and epsilon 0.001. The elapsed-time gain instead uses tuned epsilon 0.01.

For Fixup, smaller residual-branch initialization slows learning, larger initialization fails, and scalar biases improve training. Default-hyperparameter ImageNet training is fast and stable; with additional strong regularization, reducing scalar-multiplier and bias rates by 10× is beneficial. NF-ResNet stability changes with regularization and rate. In shifted-ReLU residual networks, retaining final BN permits the baseline recipe; on CIFAR, output temperature approximately 30–100 permits baseline-like training with the same high initial learning rate after internal BN removal. This is qualitative recipe compatibility, without matched accuracy trajectories. Specialized binary-network replacements can also support training after BN removal.

The i.i.d. ResNet-20/FedAvg comparison benefits from BN. With non-i.i.d. clients, mismatched local and global BN statistics and gradients introduce the analyzed convergence penalty and nonvanishing bias.

method_sensitivity.factor: Depth and optimizer in feedback alignment
method_sensitivity.what: Feedback-alignment performance and convergence vary with depth, BN, optimizer and their combination. In four-convolutional-layer ReLU CNNs on CIFAR-10, the favorable BN comparison uses separately tuned SGD or AdamW recipes. Figure 4B measures test accuracy over training steps: BN models converge earlier with smoother curves. Training uses a 50,000-step budget with early stopping for convergence or failed runs; no numerical convergence-speed comparison is stated.
